title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover ordering
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer backoff ordering to prevent thrashing during regional failover and improve load-shedding stability. No API changes. Deploy to all regions with canary first.
description: Motivation: production incidents over the last 48 hours exposed an edge case where the SLO enforcer's backoff ordering could cause cascading circuit-breaker thrashing during cross-region failover, leading to sustained 5xxs and elevated latency. This hotfix tightens the backoff ordering, adds a brief deterministic jitter window, and ensures load-shedding decisions are stable during regional handovers. Summary of changes: 1) Reordered backoff state machine to prefer exponential backoff with a short deterministic jitter to avoid synchronized retries. 2) Added a region-stability gate that delays aggressive failover-driven load shedding for 3s while connections drain. 3) Fixed ordering bug where per-route priority could be reset during fallback, causing transient overload of cheaper backends. 4) Added metrics and tracing spans for SLO enforcer decisions to aid post-incident analysis. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced failure in local canary harness - [x] Unit tests updated - [x] Integration tests for regional failover added - [x] Load test (2x baseline) passes on canary - [x] Observability dashboards updated - [x] Rollout plan approved by SRE Risks: small increase in tail latency during the 3s region-stability window; mitigated by conservative default thresholds and gradual rollout. Rollback: revert squash merge commit and redeploy canary. See linked tickets.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can you explain why deterministic jitter is preferred vs randomized jitter? Concern: might sync on similar clocks. Author: deterministic jitter here is deterministic per-backend id to break global sync while remaining reproducible for debugging.
Li Wei: We saw a related race in the fallback ordering. Is the preserve-priority fix covered by tests? Author: yes, added integration test that simulates simultaneous region drain and fallback.
Aisha Patel: CI flaky on canary e2e. Suggest adding a short retry in the test harness. Author: added retry wrapper and increased timeouts; reran tests.
Daniel Kim: Approving for merge after CI green and canary load test results. Aisha Patel: Approved.
ci_checks: integration: pass (reran after test timeout fix)
testing_notes: Local repro: used perf-canary with regional-failover scenario and reproduced thrash in previous enforcer implementation
Unit tests: state machine transition coverage increased from 62% to 88%
Integration: test_regional_failover simulates 3-region failover with staggered drains
Load test: 2x baseline sustained for 10 minutes on canary with no 5xx spike
Canary observation: small 0.3% increase in p95 for 3s during region handoff, within acceptable threshold
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: brief increase in tail latency during region-stability window. Mitigation: conservative default of 3s and feature flag to tune per-customer.
Risk: behaviour change under extreme sustained overload. Mitigation: rollback plan and metric alerts tied to error budget burn.
Risk: potential for synchronized retries if jitter flawed. Mitigation: deterministic jitter keyed by backend id and coverage in unit tests.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy to canary region (us-west-2) at 5% traffic for 30 minutes
Stage 2: Monitor SLOs and error budgets for 1 hour, check enforcer decision traces
Stage 3: Gradual increase to 25% then 50% over 2 hours if stable
Stage 4: Full global rollout with 15-minute guard rails and on-call SRE oversight
